target_customer: Young, mobile-first retail banking customers in Kenya, with a stated ambition across Africa
problem: Young Africans pay 5 to 15 percent fees to move money and lack modern banking; Fingo promised accounts opened in minutes with cheap transfers.
business_model: Neobank: fees, interchange and interest spread, delivered with a licensed partner bank

founders.name: Ian Njuguna
previous_startups: Outdoor advertising automation software for digital billboards

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile banking app with M-PESA integration and partner-bank core, plus Central Bank of Kenya approval; standard fintech engineering with regulatory dependency.

defensibility.rationale: Partnering with Ecobank and CBK approval gave some licensing position, but mobile money and other neobanks were close substitutes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ecobank became the partner bank; the acquirer, if any, is not identified in sources found.

market_need_then: Large unbanked and underbanked young population in Kenya and high remittance and transfer fees as stated by the company; mobile money was ubiquitous.

identity.visual_style: Yellow Ubuntu card (physical card marked coming soon)
identity.voice_and_tone: Youth oriented; Fingo Coins rewards and Fingo Tribe community named on the site

branding.brand_signature: Fingo Tribe community and Fingo Coins rewards
branding.community_and_virality: Site names a Fingo Tribe community; no outside coverage of it found.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch press covered the product, not the brand; some community branding on the company's own site only.

pivots.to: Kenya-first neobank launched with Ecobank Kenya as partner bank
pivots.why: Regulated product powered by a licensed bank per launch coverage

outcome_analysis: Fingo went through YC in Summer 2021, raised a reported 4 million dollar seed led by HOF Capital late in 2022 and launched in May 2023 with Ecobank Kenya, with CBK approval. YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or terms were found, so the real outcome and cause of the exit are not public in sources seen.
notes: YC directory says Acquired but one search found no acquisition; the live site shows no ownership change. Exit type follows directory status with null acquirer and date. Seed amount from TechCrunch and Business Daily; the 200k pre-seed and 7.92M total (Extruct, CB Insights) are single aggregator figures, unverified. Seed date approximated as late 2022 from May 2023 article. Competition empty: only 2023-era sources found. Some aggregator lists a fourth founder (James da Costa), not on YC page.
